summary: Ships a linux/arm64 Go binary that opens a remote PTY shell over WebSocket/WebRTC to relay.sextant.top
details: The tarball's sole payload is a ~12 MB linux/arm64 Go ELF at bin/sxt. Its imports and string table show a remote-shell agent: pion/webrtc/v4 and coder/websocket for transport, skip2/go-qrcode for controller pairing, and exec.Command + pty.Start spawning /bin/sh or bash. The binary carries hardcoded control endpoints wss://relay.sextant.top and https://relay.sextant.top, along with strings referencing signaling, c2., and systemd persistence. When the binary is executed (by a parent CLI wrapper or directly), a remote operator at relay.sextant.top drives an interactive PTY shell on the host over a WebSocket signaling channel and a WebRTC data channel — the standard remote-shell backdoor shape. Provenance corroborates intent: package.json declares `license: SEE LICENSE IN https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control`, pointing to a repository literally named `claude_control` under a `ddos`-prefixed handle not associated with a known vendor.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
